1.plans: Explore the price range step by step to map out demand and profit. Round 1: 2.8 (near the middle). Round 2: 3.5 if demand looks strong, or 2.2 if it looks weak. Round 3: 3.0–3.2 or 1.8, depending on how rounds 1 and 2 compare. After that, use a golden-section or local search around the most profitable price, moving by about 0.1–0.2. Every so often, re-test prices next to the current best one to check whether demand has shifted or there are hidden effects (for example, competitors reacting or demand depending on time). Record each price with its quantity sold and profit.
1.insights: Each unit costs 1.0 and the most any customer will pay is 4.51. Profit per round is (price − 1) × quantity sold. With no data so far, a guess based on linear demand would put the best price around (1 + 4.51)/2 ≈ 2.75. Still to be tested: how sensitive buyers are to price, and whether demand stays the same over time or depends on earlier prices.
